candidateActorIdentity: Pin the reviewed source commit and all executed build hashes before launch; never change the frozen actor or reuse a mutated runtime as initial state.
treatment: Once after planning and before requesting the prepared frame, explicitly drain, validate and learn waiting-time passive windows. The existing callback still learns newer real windows before its fresh forecast and exact-frame check. The selected action, search, motor and decision budgets do not change. All phases share duplicate/conflict and chronology checks, including frozen sessions.

preparationWait.wallTimeQualification: A JavaScript timer is not a hard real-time bound; report every observed wait and overrun, including timeout outcomes, without excluding slow attempts.

decisionRule: Archive the one candidate launch regardless of outcome. More than 8 actual executions in a complete 32-decision sample supports improved availability for this ordered development pair only. All other cases remain negative or incomplete, without retry or budget extension. Calibration coverage and goal result are separate.
preserve: all failures and any launch deviation
limitations: One ordered development pair does not estimate a general causal speedup.
Different live timing can change later trajectories and learning costs even with an identical initial state.
Recorded receipts establish represented preparations and motor attempts; software tests and source review establish that an aborted pending wait cannot trigger an invisible retry.
This short peaceful experiment cannot establish useful retention, transfer, sustained autonomous learning or open multistage capability. Those remain separate subsequent tasks.
Additional flush changes passive-window segmentation and model trajectory; do not attribute differences solely to computational cost placement.
windowSegmentation: This drain flushes the partially accumulated real passive window, so it can split nonoverlapping passive intervals, change measured passive cue durations and change the learned trajectory. It is not an exact-model-equivalent cost optimization. Every raw interval and source window is preserved; no replay or duplicate is counted as a new independent window. Report active/passive window counts and both off-critical and callback costs.
